svg.text: x and y in mm from the plate's top-left corner, as the computer is used
Plate hole used by this build: a screw through the board into a standoff.
Plate hole for a printed part.
Plate hole this build doesn't use.
Corners go on all four corners of the plate.
The VGA Adapter fits the notch in the board's top edge and fastens to the board, not the plate, at (125.75,
22) and (171.75, 22). The Reset Button sits in its hole in the top and takes no hardware.
The ACE CF Adapter has an optional top, ACE CF Adapter Top. This drawing and its hardware count are for the
The board's two spare M2 holes and the plate's under them, under the keyboard, are there in case the
keyboard ever needs support. Nothing goes in them.
ACE Board Rev 1.0 has the same holes as Rev 1.1.
The plate is a stack of three 3 mm acrylic layers, each cut from Plate.svg.
The SVG is drawn 1:1, so it can be printed at full size to check a plate.
A normal hole, from the bottom up: an M3 × 12 pan head through the back of the plate, a female-male
standoff, the board, a female-female standoff, the top, and an M3 × 6 pan head.
A CF Adapter hole has half the stack and no top: an M3 × 12 pan head through the back of the plate, a
female-female standoff, the adapter, and an M3 × 6 pan head.
Corners: an M3 × 16 countersunk screw from the top, through the plate, into a nut in the Corner's lower
VGA Adapter: an M3 × 6 pan head down through the board at each end, into a nut in the adapter.
Rubber feet: one in the Ø10 recess under each Corner.
Looking down on the plate, as the computer is used. All dimensions in mm.
